chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam informed us, he said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik narrated to us, he said: 'Abbad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn Salim narrated from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) that he said:

The master of this matter is the youngest of us in age and the most obscure in appearance. I asked: When will that be? He said: When the caravans go to pay homage to the young boy, at that time every holder of power raises his flag, so await the deliverance.

key_terms.أَخْمَلُنَا: The most obscure or least conspicuous in appearance
key_terms.بَيْعَةِ الْغُلَامِ: The homage/pledge to the young boy
key_terms.ذُو الصَّيْصِيَّةِ: The holder of power or authority (literally: one with a helmet)
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ: The master of the matter (referring to the Imam/Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of the appearance of the Mahdi according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) highlights the paradox of the Mahdi’s initial obscurity despite his seniority among the Imams, a theme central to Shia eschatology regarding the 'Minority' (al-Qawm al-Mustad'afun). The sign of 'delegations paying homage to a young boy' is interpreted by scholars as a period of widespread political fragmentation where multiple claimants to authority emerge, creating the conditions for the true Imam’s rise. This hadith serves as a critical marker for believers to anticipate the 'Faraj' (deliverance) amidst the chaos of competing powers.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (35) Muhammad bin Hammam narrated from Ja’far bin Muhammad bin Malik from Abbad bin Ya’qoob from Yahya bin Salim that Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as) had said:

“The man of this matter is the youngest and obscurest one of us.” Yahya asked him: “When will that (deliverance) be?” He said: “When delegations go to pay homage to a young boy and every fort (powerful chief) raises a flag (becomes independent) then you expect deliverance.” No one of the infallible imams has become imam while he is yet too young except this imam (al-Mahdi), whom Allah has granted the imamate and wisdom while he is yet a child as Jesus Christ and Yahya bin Zachariah, whom Allah has granted the Book, prophethood, knowledge and wisdom while yet children. The evidence for that is the saying of Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) “He (al-Qa’im) has aspects of four prophets…). One of them is Jesus the son of Marry (as), who has been granted wisdom, knowledge and prophethood while yet a child.
